title: Ryo Lu (Cursor): AI Turns Designers to Developers

reader_summary.headline: AI helps designers build code quickly without needing large engineering teams.
reader_summary.overview: Software creation used to split designers and engineers into separate roles with different tools. Cursor helps designers turn visual ideas into working code quickly. Humans must still provide direction and taste because AI alone cannot decide what looks good.

key_points.text: Cursor lets mockups in Figma become living products in minutes without a large team.
key_points.evidence_quote: When mockups that used to die in Figma can suddenly become living products in minutes.

key_points.text: AI acts as a universal helper that understands different files and connects ideas to the code base.
key_points.evidence_quote: It can talk to Figma, the mox that I had. It can talk to notion, all the ideas, the docs, the meeting notes, anything.

key_points.text: Humans must provide their own opinion because AI alone cannot decide what looks good or is right.
key_points.evidence_quote: There needs to be something for the human to specify what is good, what is right, how I want to do it.

key_points.text: Human taste acts as a filter that chooses what is good while AI handles the baseline work.
key_points.evidence_quote: the thing on top is taste or like your self-selection of what is good like you're kind of drawing the boundary that is your decision though the AI can increasingly help you do that

key_points.text: Giving vague instructions to AI agents often results in poor output without human direction.
key_points.evidence_quote: if you don't put in that opinion it will just produce AI Slop

notes: Ryo Lu spent years watching his designs die in meetings. Then he discovered the tool that lets designers ship code at the speed of thought: Cursor, the company where Ryo is now Head of Design. In this episode, a16z General Partner Jennifer Li sits down with Ryo to discuss why "taste" is the wrong framework for understanding the future, why purposeful apps are "selfish," how System 7 holds secrets about AI interfaces, and the radical bet that one codebase can serve everyone if you design the concepts right instead of the buttons.
